topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: The syllabus must state GenAI policy for relevant assessed components. An individual assessment may override it when communicated with the assessment specifications.
topics.scope: From Term 1, 2025–26; read the specific assessment instructions before using GenAI.

claims.text: The syllabus must state GenAI policy for relevant assessed components. An individual assessment may override it when communicated with the assessment specifications.

evidence.quote: Starting Term 1, 2025-2026, every course must include an explicit declaration of AI usage policies in a dedicated section of the syllabus with the heading Generative AI Use Policy.
evidence.title: Policies on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: Disclose the tool and how much it influenced the output. A separate statement is unnecessary when disclosure is already embedded or the specified activity makes the use obvious.
topics.scope: Faculty and students; additional course disclosure requirements must be properly communicated with the activity specifications.

claims.text: Disclose the tool and how much it influenced the output. A separate statement is unnecessary when disclosure is already embedded or the specified activity makes the use obvious.

evidence.quote: For both faculty and students, the use of generative AI in the production of any material, presentation, or submission, must be accompanied by a written disclosure statement.
evidence.title: Policies on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education

claims.text: Disclose the tool and how much it influenced the output. A separate statement is unnecessary when disclosure is already embedded or the specified activity makes the use obvious.

evidence.quote:
A separate disclosure statement is not required anymore if the disclosure is already
           embedded within the output itself (e.g., if the generative AI was used as part of a research
           methodology, and this was already explained in the Methodology section of the
           manuscript). Likewise, a separate disclosure statement is not required anymore if the type


                                 of generative AI use is already obvious from the specifications of the activity (e.g., the
                                 activity requires students to use generative AI for a specific purpose).

                            •
evidence.title: Policies on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education

topics.evidenceScope: Faculty and students; additional course disclosure requirements must be properly communicated with the activity specifications.

topics.title: Privacy and data
topics.summary: Personal or highly sensitive information, internal university documents, proprietary research and confidential information should never be shared with GenAI services.
topics.scope: The policy uses “should never” for these data categories; research participant data has additional consent and anonymisation conditions.

topics.summary: The policy names tools as examples but does not establish a university licence, free access or universal assessment approval.
topics.scope: No independently published institutional tool records were found in the frozen public tool collection.

topics.title: Research and publication
topics.summary: Research participant data use must be declared in informed consent, anonymised, and ethically approved when necessary; venue-specific disclosure requirements also apply.
topics.scope: Research data and publication-specific conditions; this is not blanket permission to upload confidential research.

claims.text: Research participant data use must be declared in informed consent, anonymised, and ethically approved when necessary; venue-specific disclosure requirements also apply.

evidence.quote: In research, if any participant or subject data is to be processed by generative AI services, this must be indicated in the informed consent form in the data collection process. Furthermore, such data must always be anonymized, and ethical approval must be secured when necessary.
evidence.title: Policies on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education

claims.text: Research participant data use must be declared in informed consent, anonymised, and ethically approved when necessary; venue-specific disclosure requirements also apply.

evidence.quote:

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity

additionalTopics.scope: GenAI-related dishonesty; separate plagiarism-detection functions are not conflated with AI detection.

additionalTopics.title: Teaching guidance
additionalTopics.summary: Teachers must communicate assessment-specific overrides and any extra disclosure requirements when releasing the activity specifications.
additionalTopics.scope: Course and activity instructions; no automatic misconduct finding follows from a detector flag.

evidence.title: Policies on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education
evidence.location: IV.c Assessment exception; physical PDF page 6

claims.text: Teachers must communicate assessment-specific overrides and any extra disclosure requirements when releasing the activity specifications.

evidence.quote:
Instructors may include additional disclosure requirements for students in specific course
                                 activities or assessments. These must be properly communicated to the students upon the
                                 release of the activity or assessment specifications. Examples of additional disclosure
                                 requirements are: (1) disclosure of relevant interaction logs of the student with the
                                 generative AI (e.g., prompts used, response of the AI), and (2) compliance with a specific
                                 format for citation (e.g., APA4, MLE5, or a custom format for the course).
